test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 01 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about uniform motion?

options.text: The body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time
The speed varies continuously with time

solution:
The correct answer is __**The speed varies continuously with time**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform motion** is defined as the motion in which a body covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, irrespective of how small these time intervals are. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• In uniform motion, the **velocity remains constant** throughout the motion because the direction and magnitude of velocity do not change. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The **acceleration** in uniform motion is zero because there is no change in velocity over time. This means the object maintains a constant speed in a straight line. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The statement "**The speed varies continuously with time**" contradicts the definition of uniform motion, as the speed must remain constant for the motion to be considered uniform. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Uniform motion typically occurs in idealized conditions, such as when an object moves in space without being subjected to external forces like friction or air resistance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Uniform Motion:**

 
 
• The object moves along a **straight path** without any deviation.
 
• The distance traveled by the object is directly proportional to the time elapsed.
 
• The motion is characterized by a **zero net acceleration**, implying no forces are acting to change the velocity of the object.
 
• Examples include a car moving with cruise control on a straight highway or a satellite orbiting Earth at a constant speed.
 
 
 
• **Relation Between Speed, Velocity, and Acceleration:**
 
 
• **Speed** is a scalar quantity that measures the rate of change of distance.
 
• **Velocity** is a vector quantity that includes both speed and direction.
 
• **Acceleration** is the rate of change of velocity. For uniform motion, acceleration is zero as velocity remains constant.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Non-Uniform Motion:**
 
 
• A car accelerating on a road, where its speed increases or decreases over time.
 
• A ball thrown upward, which slows down as it rises and speeds up as it falls due to gravitational force.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion (For Uniform Acceleration):**
 
 
• **v = u + at:** Final velocity (v) is the initial velocity (u) plus acceleration (a) multiplied by time (t).
 
• **s = ut + 0.5at²:** Displacement (s) is the sum of the initial velocity multiplied by time and half of the acceleration multiplied by the square of time.
 
• **v² = u² + 2as:** Relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Real-life Applications of Uniform Motion:**

 
 
• In astronomy, planets exhibit nearly uniform motion in their orbits over short time intervals.
 
• Trains moving at constant speeds on straight tracks serve as practical examples of uniform motion.
 
 
 
• **Misconceptions:**
 
 
• Uniform motion does not imply the absence of motion. It simply indicates the absence of acceleration.
 
• Uniform motion does not apply to circular paths, as the direction of velocity changes continuously, leading to acceleration (centripetal acceleration).
